name: Thomas Hunt
title: Associate Professor, Department of Kinesiology and Health Education
research_summary: Thomas M. Hunt, J.D., Ph.D. , is an associate professor in the Department of Kinesiology and Health Education at The University of Texas at Austin. His scholarship explores how physical culture intersects with global political affairs. A previous book of his entitled Drug Games: The International Olympic Committee and the Politics of Doping, 1960-2008 offered a critical analysis on how the history of performance-enhancement in sport was impacted by Cold War and post-Cold War politics. In his forthcoming (University of Oklahoma Press) Fight Like a Machine: The Combat Future of the Human Body , Hunt expands this focus to the defense and national security arena. In doing so, he argues that emerging technologies are redefining the role of the human body in warfare in ways that necessitate fundamental changes in the way the U.S. military recruits, trains, and plans for future conflicts. | Ph.D. , The University of Texas at Austin, 2007 J.D. , Baylor University School of Law, 2003 B.A. in Government, The University of Texas at Austin, 2000 | Examines the intersection of physical culture and international political history.

name: Tolga Ozyurtcu
title: Professor of Instruction, Department of Kinesiology and Health Education; Maxine Foreman Zarrow Endowed Faculty Fellowship in Education (Holder)
research_summary: Tolga Ozyurtcu, Ph.D., is an associate professor of instruction in the Department of Kinesiology and Health Education at The University of Texas at Austin and currently serves as the department's undergraduate coordinator. Ozyurtcu holds a B.A. in Political Science from Haverford College, an M.Sc. in Sport Management from UT Austin and a Ph.D. in Physical Culture and Sports Studies, also from UT Austin. He teaches in the areas of Sport Management and Physical Culture and Sport Studies, including classes in the management of sport organizations, media and public relations in sport, and the historical, philosophical, and ethical aspects of sport and physical activity. An experienced coach and sport industry consultant, Ozyurtcu seeks to engage his students by combining practical and theoretical approaches to the study of sport. Ozyurtcu's research interests include the history of sporting subcultures, sport and cultural geography, physical culture history and innovation in sport. name: Veronica Yan
title: Associate Professor, Department of Educational Psychology; Joe R. & Teresa Lozano Long Endowed Faculty Fellows Fund (Holder)
research_summary: Bridging social, cognitive and educational psychology fields, my research explores how we can empower people to become motivated and effectively self-regulated learners. Learners must have the right mindset (e.g., they must be motivated and interpret the experience of difficulty in productive ways) but they also have to know effective strategies for learning. Rather than "making learning easy," what research from cognitive psychology demonstrates is that the effective learning strategies that make learning stick are often the ones that introduce difficulties (e.g., interleaving, retrieval practice, pre-testing). I am presently focused on examining the mechanisms underlying these "desirably difficult" strategies and the motivational mindsets that encourage learners to not just study harder but to study smarter. name: Xiao Liu
title: Assistant Professor, Department of Educational Psychology; Pearson Endowed Faculty Fellowship in Psychometrics (Holder)
research_summary: Xiao Liu's research focuses on developing and applying statistical methods for causal inference in observational or randomized studies. This includes causal mediation analysis, causal inference with machine learning methods, longitudinal or clustered data analyses, study design (e.g., sample size calculation and statistical power analysis), and sensitivity analysis methods.
